from.q: What age can my child join?
from.a: Play Group is for 2 – 3 years, Nursery for 3 – 4 years, Junior KG for 4 – 5 years and Senior KG for 5 – 6 years. Day care welcomes children from 2 to 8 years.

A Montessori-based, thematic curriculum through our Foundational Development Program. By Senior KG it is aligned with State, CBSE and ICSE board requirements, so children are ready for mainstream school.

Timings differ from branch to branch, and some programs run in more than one batch. You’ll find each branch’s programs, batches and timings on its page, under Branches. Day care follows on after class, so children can move from class straight into day care.

from.q: Can children from other schools join day care?
from.a: Yes. Day care is open to Crossmaze children and to children from other schools, and we pick them up from a nearby drop point of their school.

from.q: Can I see my child during the day?
from.a: Yes. Parents get live CCTV access, and the Crossmaze Care parents’ app keeps you updated on your child’s day.
Yes. Our in-house transport runs on set routes within a 5 km radius of each centre. Seats depend on availability, so please check with your nearest centre.

from.q: How do I apply for admission?
from.a: Send us an enquiry, call us or message us on WhatsApp. Our admissions team will answer your questions and arrange a visit to your nearest centre, where you can meet the centre head and complete the admission.

to.q: What age can my child join?
to.a: Children join the class that fits their age on 1 June: Play Group from 2 years, Nursery from 3, Junior KG from 4 and Senior KG from 5. Day care welcomes children from 2 to 8 years, with or without a Crossmaze class.
A Montessori-based, thematic curriculum: our Foundational Development Program, which brings language, numbers, social skills and physical development together in every theme.

Timings differ from branch to branch, and some programs run in more than one batch. You’ll find each branch’s programs, batches and timings on its page, under Branches. Day care follows on after class, so children can move from class straight into day care.

to.q: Do children bring their own food?
to.a: Yes. Children bring a packed snack from home, and children in day care bring a packed lunch too.

to.q: Can children from other schools join day care?
to.a: Yes. Day care is open to children up to 8 years from other schools. We collect them from the nearest drop point of their school bus.

to.q: Can I see my child during the day?
to.a: The Crossmaze Care parents’ app keeps every parent updated on their child’s day, and day care parents can also watch live on CCTV.
Yes. Our in-house transport runs on set routes within a 5 km radius of each centre. Seats depend on availability, so please check with your nearest centre.

to.q: How do I apply for admission?
to.a: Send us an enquiry, call us or message us on WhatsApp. Our admissions team will answer your questions and arrange a visit to your nearest centre, where you can meet the centre head and complete the admission.

from: Play Group is one of the most delightful ways for your child to begin a journey of discovery. It is a place to learn about the world, make friends and practise essential social skills, and an enriching experience for parents, grandparents and caregivers too.

Our Play Group sessions support physical development, encourage problem-solving, build communication and nurture positive social interaction, with every moment full of joy. Our qualified staff create a safe space where children aged two and above explore, learn and play together.

Our Play Group sessions support physical development, encourage problem-solving, build communication and nurture positive social interaction, with every moment full of joy. Our qualified staff create a safe space where children aged two and above explore, learn and play together.
Children don’t need to be toilet trained to join: our staff change nappies and help each child with toilet training.

from: Junior KG is a pivotal year in which we nurture every side of a child’s development. Our curriculum focuses on the key areas that lay the foundation for a bright future: numeracy, literacy, fine motor skills, logical thinking and problem-solving.

At this age children are refining their language and thinking skills, are eager to explore new languages and are developing a keen sense of numbers. Through engaging group activities, our teachers encourage teamwork, participation, sharing and taking turns.
